summary_ja: 事業法人等向けエクスポージャーのLGD(先進的手法の推計値、基礎的手法の規定値、担保による削減効果の算式と運用要件、下限値、準用規定)を定める。
summary_en: Sets LGD for corporate, etc. exposures: own estimates under the advanced approach, supervisory values under the foundation approach, collateral recognition formulas and operational requirements, and LGD floors.
paragraphs: The LGD used by an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets and in calculating expected loss for corporate, etc. exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied shall be an estimate, expressed as a percentage, of the ratio of the economic loss arising at default on that corporate, etc. exposure to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied to EAD.

The LGD used by an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets and in calculating expected loss for corporate, etc. exposures shall be the value specified in each of the following items according to the category of exposure listed in that item; provided, however, that in the case of subordinated claims, it shall be 75%. (i) Sovereign exposures: 45%. (ii) Exposures to regulated financial institutions and unregulated financial institutions, etc.: 45%. (iii) Corporate exposures (excluding exposures to regulated financial institutions and unregulated financial institutions, etc.): 40%.

Notwithstanding the preceding paragraph, where eligible receivables collateral, eligible real estate collateral or eligible other asset collateral (hereinafter referred to as "eligible asset collateral") or eligible financial collateral has been established on a corporate, etc. exposure (excluding subordinated claims), an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach may take into account the effect of credit risk mitigation techniques by the following formula; provided, however, that where the corporate, etc. exposure is a repo-style transaction, margin lending or a similar overseas transaction and the credit risk mitigation effect of eligible financial collateral is taken into account, EAD shall be calculated under paragraph (2) of the following Article, and the value provided in item (i) or (ii) of the preceding paragraph shall be used for LGD. {{F:p166i0}} LGD* is the LGD taking into account the effect of credit risk mitigation techniques. LGD_{U} is the value set according to the category of exposure listed in the items of the preceding paragraph. The same applies in paragraph (6). LGD_{S} is the value set in the table of the following paragraph according to the category of collateral asset listed in that table. E is the exposure amount. The same applies in paragraphs (6) and (8) and Article 141, paragraph (3). E_{S} is the value calculated as C·(1 − H_{C} − H_{fx}) (in this case, the upper limit of E_{S} is E·(1 + H_{E})). The same applies in paragraphs (6) and (8) and Article 141, paragraph (3). C is the present value of the collateral received. The same applies in paragraph (6). H_{C} is the haircut set in the table of the following paragraph according to the category of collateral asset listed in that table. The same applies in paragraph (6). H_{fx} is the haircut applied under Section 6, Subsection 3 of the preceding Chapter where the currencies of the exposure and the eligible asset collateral differ. The same applies in paragraph (6). H_{E} is the haircut applied under Section 6, Subsection 3 of the preceding Chapter according to the type of asset delivered to the counterparty where the exposure falls under item (vii) of the table in Article 45, paragraph (1). The same applies in paragraphs (6) and (8) and Article 141, paragraph (3).

Where the formula in the preceding paragraph is used, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach shall use the LGD_{S} and haircuts set out in the following table according to the category of collateral asset listed in that table. {{T:p167t0}}

In order to take into account the effect of credit risk mitigation techniques under paragraph (3), an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach shall satisfy, for eligible asset collateral or eligible financial collateral that secures a corporate, etc. exposure (excluding subordinated claims), the following operational requirements according to the type of collateral. (i) The operational requirements for the claim that is the object of eligible receivables collateral (hereinafter referred to in this item as "eligible receivables") are the following: (a) The legal framework under which the collateral is provided is robust, and the creditor's rights in respect of the eligible receivables or their sale proceeds are secured. (b) All steps necessary for the enforcement of the security interest have been taken. (c) The contract concerning the establishment of the collateral enables enforcement in accordance with its terms in the jurisdictions relevant to the collateral, and legally and effectively binds the contracting parties. (d) The requirement in (c) is based on sufficient legal research and legal reasoning, and its enforceability is confirmed in a timely manner to be continuously maintained. (e) The establishment of the security interest is properly documented, and clear and robust procedures are in place for the timely collection of the eligible receivables or their proceeds. (f) Robust procedures are in place for assessing the credit risk of the receivables that are the object of the collateral. (g) Where the assessment of the credit risk of the obligor of the eligible receivables (hereinafter referred to in this item as the "third-party obligor") depends on the obligor of the secured claim, the credit extension policy of the obligor of the secured claim is verified in ascertaining the soundness and creditworthiness of the third-party obligor. (h) The difference between the amount of the secured claim and the amount of the eligible receivables fully reflects collection costs, the degree of concentration of a single third-party obligor in the pool of eligible receivables, concentration risk within the total exposures of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach, and all other factors to be taken into account. (i) The secured claim is appropriately and continuously monitored. (ii) The operational requirements for the real estate that is the object of eligible real estate collateral (hereinafter referred to in this item as "eligible real estate") are the following: (a) The security interest is lawfully and validly established in the relevant jurisdictions, is enforceable in accordance with the terms of the contract establishing the collateral, and is registered in a timely and appropriate manner. (b) A contract concerning the establishment of the collateral, and legal procedures for enforcing that contract, are in place such that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach can realize the collateral value within a reasonable period. (c) The appraised value of the eligible real estate does not exceed its fair market value as of the valuation date. (d) The collateral value of the eligible real estate is assessed at least once a year, and where there is information indicating that the collateral value of the eligible real estate collateral has declined significantly, or where default or another credit event occurs, the real estate is valued by a real estate appraiser or a person recognized as having sufficient accuracy in valuing collateral. (e) Documents clarifying the type of eligible real estate and the policy for extending credit secured by eligible real estate (including, but not limited to, reflection in terms such as interest rates) are maintained. (f) Measures are in place to appropriately protect the eligible real estate from damage and deterioration. (g) The amount and content of legally valid claims that rank prior to the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach (including senior security interests) on the eligible real estate are continuously monitored. (h) The risk of liabilities relating to environmental protection arising from the eligible real estate is appropriately monitored. (i) Where a subordinated security interest satisfying the requirement in (a) has been established, the amount obtained by deducting from the collateral value that takes the haircut into account the exposure amounts of all holders of senior security interests (hereinafter referred to in this sub-item as the "collateral value after taking senior security interests into account") shall be the collateral value of the eligible real estate. In this case, where there are holders of security interests of the same rank, the amount obtained by pro-rating the collateral value after taking senior security interests into account according to the amounts secured by the security interests of those holders of the same rank shall be the collateral value of the eligible real estate. (iii) The operational requirements for the asset that is the object of eligible other asset collateral (hereinafter referred to in this item as "eligible other assets") are the following requirements: (a) The requirements listed in (a) through (h) of the preceding item are satisfied. In this case, in those provisions the term "eligible real estate collateral" shall be read as "eligible other asset collateral", "real estate" as "asset", "eligible real estate" as "eligible other assets", "registered" as "the perfection requirements are satisfied", "a real estate appraiser or a person recognized as having sufficient accuracy in valuing collateral" as "a person recognized as having sufficient accuracy in valuing collateral", and "legally valid claims that rank prior (including senior security interests)" as "legally valid claims that rank prior". (b) The security interest is first-ranking. (c) The contract concerning the establishment of eligible other asset collateral states the details of the collateral, the right of inspection, and that the collateral value will be revalued at the request of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach. (d) The credit risk management policy states the types of collateral that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach evaluates, the policy for determining an appropriate collateral amount according to the exposure amount, and the method of operating that policy, and is maintained so that it can be used for internal audit or external audit. (e) A policy for extending credit secured by eligible other assets is established, and that policy takes into account the amount of collateral to be secured according to the exposure amount, the ability of that Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach to promptly dispose of the collateral, its ability to objectively set the disposable price or market price, the frequency with which an expert valuation or appraisal or other valuation can be promptly obtained, and the range within which the valuation of the collateral fluctuates. (f) In periodic valuation procedures, particular attention is paid so that, for assets with characteristics susceptible to fashion, downward adjustments are made that take into account the decline in asset value accompanying changes in fashion or obsolescence, and not merely a decline in physical useful life or deterioration. (g) Where raw materials, work in progress, finished goods, automobile dealers' inventory or other inventory, or machinery and equipment is taken as collateral, physical inspection of the collateral is carried out in the periodic valuation procedures. (iv) The operational requirements for the assets that are the object of eligible financial collateral are those provided in Article 59, Articles 62 through 64, Article 66 and Articles 106 through 108.

Notwithstanding paragraphs (2) and (3), where multiple items of collateral satisfying the operational requirements provided in the items of the preceding paragraph according to the category of collateral asset have been established on a corporate, etc. exposure, the effect of credit risk mitigation techniques may be taken into account by the following formula. {{F:p169i0}} LGD** is the LGD taking into account the effect of credit risk mitigation techniques of the multiple items of collateral. i denotes the category of collateral asset of the established collateral, and means eligible financial collateral, eligible receivables collateral, eligible real estate collateral or eligible other asset collateral. {{F:p170i0}} is the LGD_{S} set under paragraph (4) according to the category of collateral asset of the established collateral. {{F:p170i1}} is the value calculated as C·(1 − H_{C} − H_{fx}) according to the category of collateral asset of the established collateral; provided, however, that where {{F:p170i2}} exceeds E·(1 + H_{E}), the value shall be adjusted, with the C·(1 − H_{C} − H_{fx}) calculated according to the category of collateral asset of that collateral as the upper limit, so that {{F:p170i3}} equals E·(1 + H_{E}).

Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the estimated LGD used in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets and in calculating expected loss for corporate exposures that fall under corporate, etc. exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied (hereinafter referred to in this Article and the following Article as "corporate exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied") shall not be lower than 25%.

Notwithstanding the preceding paragraph, where eligible financial collateral or eligible asset collateral has been established on a corporate exposure to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach may set the floor of the estimated LGD used in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets and in calculating expected loss for that exposure at the value, calculated by the following formula, that takes into account the effect of credit risk mitigation techniques. {{F:p170i4}} LGD_{floor} is the floor of the LGD estimate taking into account the effect of credit risk mitigation techniques. LGD_{Ufloor} is 25%. LGD_{Sfloor} is the value set in the table of the following paragraph according to the category of collateral asset listed in that table.

Where the formula in the preceding paragraph is used, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach shall use, as LGD_{Sfloor}, the value specified in the lower column of the following table according to the category of collateral asset listed in that table. {{T:p170t0}}

The provisions of paragraph (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis where the effect of credit risk mitigation techniques is taken into account in the LGD floor under paragraph (8). In this case, the term "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach" in paragraph (5) shall be read as "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach", and "corporate, etc. exposure (excluding subordinated claims)" as "corporate exposure to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied".

Where a corporate, etc. exposure to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied is a repo-style transaction, margin lending or a similar overseas transaction and the credit risk mitigation effect of eligible financial collateral is taken into account, EAD shall be calculated under paragraph (2) of the following Article, and an LGD that does not take into account the credit risk mitigation effect of collateral shall be used.

The provisions of paragraphs (2) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach sets the LGD used in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets and in calculating expected loss for corporate, etc. exposures that do not fall under corporate, etc. exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied. In this case, the term "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach" in those provisions shall be read as "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach", and "corporate, etc. exposure" as "corporate, etc. exposure (excluding corporate, etc. exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied)".

The provisions of paragraphs (2) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis where, in some business units or asset categories among corporate, etc. exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied, the minimum requirements provided in the following Section for the estimation of LGD are not satisfied, and the LGD used in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets and in calculating expected loss for the exposures included in that business unit or asset category is set. In this case, the term "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach" in those provisions shall be read as "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach".

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach satisfies the minimum requirements provided in the following Section for the estimation of the LGD applied only to those exposures among corporate, etc. exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied on which no collateral has been established (including, for exposures partially secured by collateral, the portion not secured by collateral), it may use the estimated LGD in the formula for the amount of credit risk-weighted assets and in calculating expected loss for those exposures on which no collateral has been established. In this case, the effect of collateral shall not be taken into account in estimating LGD, and the LGD of corporate exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied shall not be lower than 25%.

The provisions of paragraphs (3) through (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis where, in the case of the preceding paragraph, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach estimates the LGD of corporate, etc. exposures to which the advanced internal ratings-based approach can be applied on which eligible financial collateral or eligible asset collateral has been established. In this case, the term "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the foundation internal ratings-based approach" in those provisions shall be read as "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the advanced internal ratings-based approach", and the phrase "is the value set according to the category of exposure listed in the items of the preceding paragraph. The same applies in paragraph (6)." in paragraph (3) shall be read as "is the estimated LGD applied to exposures on which no collateral has been established (including, for exposures partially secured by collateral, the portion not secured by collateral)".

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach shall not take credit risk mitigation effects into account using the simple approach provided in Section 6, Subsection 4 of the preceding Chapter.
